correctness.rationale: For K_{a,2}, the case split on whether the two B-agents share a block is exhaustive. Payoff comparisons reduce to strict density inequalities; all one-B and two-B blockers are classified or subsumed, yielding necessary and sufficient phase criteria and exact minimum sizes. Simple inequalities force the global cutoff; an explicit construction attains it and yields an exact count. A separate integer-only labeled-partition brute force on a=2,...,6 passed (5287 partitions and 217392 blocking coalitions), corroborating rather than replacing the all-a proof.

value.rationale: The exact universal coalition-size threshold distinguishes full core stability from q-size relaxations on a nontrivial two-type graph family and is sharp for every order. Complete phase criteria and the polynomial-count, exponentially rare sharpness construction quantify a motivated gap between the existence of blocking groups, the number of people needed to coordinate, and uniform random-blocker detection.
